177: Whether Commerce properly applied adverse facts available and assigned the 25.76% Vietnam-wide rate after Grobest failed to cooperate

We find that substantial evidence supports Commerce's determination that the 25.76% Vietnam-wide rate was appropriate to ensure Grobest did not benefit from refusing to cooperate with Commerce's requests for complete information regarding its affiliations, sales of subject merchandise, and factors of production.
690: Commerce's application of adverse facts available and selection of the $2.63/kg AFA rate from a prior review for the China-wide entity.
As to the AFA rate selected by Commerce for the China-wide entity, Commerce properly corroborated the rate by demonstrating why it was reliable and relevant.
1894: AD/CVD adverse facts available: Commerce's use of the 74.34% adverse facts available rate based on Shinkong's highest transaction-specific margin, held permissible under 19 U.S.C. 1677e(b)(4).
Commerce may use, as adverse facts available pursuant to 19 U.S.C. § 1677e(b)(4), the highest transaction-specific margin on the record of the subject review.
1927: Adverse facts available: Commerce's use of AFA to deny Hilltop a separate rate and assign the China-wide rate, based on material misrepresentations and failure to cooperate, was supported by substantial evidence.

Commerce properly applied an adverse inference because, through material misrepresentations and refusal to respond to its inquiries, Hilltop failed to cooperate by not acting to the best of its ability.
1928: Total (rather than partial) adverse facts available: Commerce properly rejected all of Hilltop's reported data as unreliable because the missing information was core and the deficiencies pervaded all submissions.

Commerce also properly applied total AFA, as opposed to partial AFA, because Hilltop's failure to disclose its affiliates and its misrepresentations undermined all of Hilltop's submissions regarding its ownership and corporate structure
1929: Corroboration of the 112.81% China-wide AFA petition rate under 19 U.S.C. 1677e(c) using Red Garden margin data and the age of the information.
Commerce properly corroborated its selection of the petition rate as the China-wide rate based on AFA.
2232: Whether Commerce could apply the PRC-wide entity rate, calculated using adverse facts available, to ATM, a cooperating respondent; the court held the AFA-based rate could be applied because ATM failed to rebut the NME presumption.

Commerce's conclusion that the PRC-wide entity is subject to an AFA-based rate logically requires Commerce to apply the same AFA-based rate to all members of the PRC-wide entity that have not proven their independence from the state, including ATM.
2425: Commerce's use of adverse inferences under 19 U.S.C. 1677e(a)-(b) to disregard Koehler's original home-market sales data after finding intentional transshipment and misrepresentation
We see no reversible error in Commerce's determination to draw adverse inferences as to Koehler without relying on Koehler's original, incorrect home-sales data.
2426: Commerce's adoption and corroboration of the 75.36% adverse rate from the petition, using Koehler's second-review sales data

We see no reversible error in Commerce's adoption of a 75.36% rate from Appvion's petition, which Commerce sufficiently corroborated using Koehler's own data (which it could assume was not skewed against Koehler).
2427: Commerce's refusal to accept Koehler's late-submitted updated home-market sales data under 19 U.S.C. 1677m(d) and (e)
We see no reversible error in Commerce's refusal to accept Koehler's revised home-market sales data.
2916: Commerce's application of adverse facts available to Borusan for failing to report HRS purchases from two mills; substantial evidence supported AFA
We agree with Maverick and the United States that substantial evidence supports Commerce's decision to apply AFA.
2918: Commerce's refusal to apply adverse facts available to the Government of Turkey for withholding HRS data and documents
We agree with Borusan and Toscelik that Commerce's decision not to apply AFA is supported by substantial evidence.
5302: Adverse facts available based on Prosperity's misreporting of yield strength: Federal Circuit reinstated Commerce's finding of misreporting and noncompliance, reversing the Trade Court's reversal; vacated that part of the judgment.
We thus conclude that the Trade Court erred when it reversed Commerce's finding that Prosperity misreported yield strength.
5336: AD adverse facts available and surrogate data reliability: whether Commerce could reject Thai Fermentation statements as incomplete and rely on subsidy-distorted Thai Ajinomoto statements, with the court holding Commerce adequately explained its choice on third redetermination.

At least as of this third redetermination by Commerce where it determined that the missing information in the untranslated financial statement was vital information and of critical importance, Commerce had adequately explained the reasoning underlying its decision to use the Thai Ajinomoto financial statements rather than the Thai Fermentation financial statements.
7992: Adverse facts available: Commerce's application of facts available and adverse inferences, and its selection of total AFA rather than partial AFA, were supported by substantial evidence and upheld, yielding the 118.04 percent margin.
The Court of International Trade correctly determined that Commerce's application of FA and AFA was supported by substantial evidence.
8176: Whether Commerce properly invoked the facts-otherwise-available provision 19 U.S.C. 1677e(a): substantial evidence supports (a)(1) and (a)(2)(D) for the FIFO-inferred sales but not (a)(2)(B) or (a)(2)(C).
We find substantial-evidence support as to two of them.
8177: Whether Commerce properly disregarded all of Bosun's country-of-origin information and applied adverse inferences; the court found the unreliability premise unexplained and remanded, limiting disregard to the FIFO-inferred sales unless reliability problems extend further.
We conclude that Commerce has not satisfactorily explained why substantial evidence supports its determination of unreliability of all of Bosun's origin information.
8181: Commerce's use of total adverse facts available (AFA)-based margins to compute the all-others rate in an administrative review; Chevron step two upheld the methodology as reasonable.
We conclude that Commerce's methodology for calculating the all-others rate was not contrary to statute and reasonable.
8182: Commerce's application of partial AFA to Dezhou's individual dumping margin based on supplier Lingyu's transshipment fraud; upheld as supported by substantial evidence and reasonable.
And it reasonably applied partial-AFA rates to mandatory respondent Dezhou based on substantial evidence that Dezhou's supplier had engaged in a fraudulent transshipment scheme.
8195: Whether Commerce properly applied total adverse facts available and the 60.81% rate; the court held the total AFA determination unsupported by substantial evidence and affirmed the zero margin based on partial neutral facts available.
Substantial evidence does not support Commerce's initial decision to disregard all of Hyundai's price information as unreliable.
8479: Whether Commerce violated 19 U.S.C. § 1677m(d) by making adverse factual findings without notice and an opportunity to cure; the court found no such error.

We agree with the CIT that there was no such error. Section 1677m(d) applies to findings based on data provided in response to a request by Commerce and not to findings based on data voluntarily submitted on a respondent's own initiative, as occurred here.
8585: Adverse facts available: Commerce's application of the highest available (114.90%) rate under 19 U.S.C. § 1677e(d)(2) was upheld as a proper case-specific evaluation.
Commerce conducted a proper evaluation under §1677e(d)(2) in applying the highest available rate.
8671: Whether Commerce's rejection of the claimed post-sale adjustment, based on the manipulation factors and concerns about legitimacy, was supported by substantial evidence and in accordance with law; the majority upheld Commerce's approach to potential manipulation.
We disagree that there must be actual manipulation of post-sale price adjustment data in order for Commerce to reject a proposed post-sale price adjustment.
8728: Commerce's application of adverse facts available (adverse inference that the Chinese government failed to cooperate and that electricity prices were subsidized) upheld as supported by substantial evidence.
Commerce is entitled to apply adverse facts available where, as here, an interested party declines to provide requested information and fails to cooperate with an investigation.
8784: Whether Commerce properly applied adverse facts available under 19 U.S.C. § 1677e(b) and selected the 33.8% rate from the petition; court held Commerce did not abuse its discretion in applying facts available with an adverse inference.
Thus, Commerce did not abuse its discretion in applying all facts available with an adverse inference.
9011: Whether Commerce properly applied adverse inferences and partial adverse facts available to Hyundai's service-related revenue, and the resulting margin increase.

Commerce has no authority to apply adverse facts and inferences unless the respondent has failed to provide requested information when notified of the deficiency, and has not acted to the best of its ability in responding to such requests.
9422: Commerce's application of total adverse facts available to Uttam Galva for failing to report an affiliated cross-owned company, under 19 U.S.C. § 1677e(a)(2) and (b).

Commerce's determination that Uttam Galva "with[held]" information from or "fail[ed] to provide" information to Commerce regarding its affiliation and cross-ownership with LSIL is accordingly supported by substantial evidence.
9980: AD/CVD adverse facts available: whether Commerce properly applied facts otherwise available and an adverse inference after finding Deacero's revised cost database unreliable and its cooperation lacking.
Accordingly, Commerce's decision to apply AFA in the selection of Deacero's AD duty rate is supported by substantial evidence and otherwise in accordance with law.
9981: AD/CVD selection and corroboration of the 40.52 percent AFA rate from the petition, including whether the rate was reliable, relevant, and not punitive.
Accordingly, Commerce's corroboration of Deacero's AFA rate is supported by substantial evidence.
10103: AD/CVD adverse facts available: Commerce properly applied adverse facts available after Habas withheld duty drawback information, and selected the 14.01 percent rate from the hierarchy of facts otherwise available.
Habas has not shown that Commerce exceeded its statutory authority in the selection of the 14.01 countervailing duty rate, we affirm.
10359: AD/CVD adverse facts available: Commerce's reliance on facts otherwise available under 19 U.S.C. 1677e(a)(1) for missing product-specific cost and cost-reconciliation information was upheld.
Commerce's determination that necessary information was missing from the record and its decision to rely on facts otherwise available were supported by substantial evidence.
10360: AD/CVD adverse inference: Commerce's selection of an adverse inference under 1677e(b) because Hyundai failed to act to the best of its ability was upheld.
Commerce's decision to use an adverse inference in selecting from among the facts otherwise available is also reasonable and supported by substantial evidence, and not contrary to law.
10397: Commerce's use of an adverse facts available (AFA) rate (Fengtai's 82.05%) in calculating the separate rate, including reliance on an AFA rate derived from a prior administrative review; court upheld the AFA-based separate rate.
Bosun's argument is expressly foreclosed by statute.
10966: Whether Commerce may carry forward an AFA-based PRC-wide NME entity rate, including adverse inferences, into a later administrative review against a cooperating exporter that failed to rebut the presumption of government control; court upheld carrying forward the AFA-based rate.
Commerce may carry forward an initial NME entity rate, including adverse inferences built into that rate, in subsequent administrative reviews.
11319: Whether the AFA-based all-others rate was presumptively representative of non-selected respondents despite the mandatory respondents' AFA rates and historical calculated rates; rate upheld
We therefore reject Appellants' arguments that the mandatory respondents' receipt of the AFA rate provides substantial evidence to undermine the presumption of representativeness.
11637: AD/CVD adverse facts available / separate rate denial: Commerce's denial of separate antidumping rates and assignment of PRC-wide rate upheld on substantial evidence of government control over management selection and export activities (de facto control factors).
Because appellants' assertions of legal error fail and Commerce's findings are supported by substantial evidence, we affirm.
13542: AD/CVD adverse facts available: Commerce's application of partial adverse facts available for failure to cooperate after Salzgitter's unreasonable-burden claim; court held Salzgitter failed to propose reasonable alternative forms under 19 U.S.C. 1677m(c)(1), though Commerce's finding of no unreasonable burden was unsupported by substantial evidence.
We conclude that Commerce's choice of adverse inference in its application of adverse facts available was supported by substantial evidence and otherwise in accordance with law.
13543: AD/CVD adverse facts available rate selection: Commerce's use of the highest non-aberrational net price among the 28,000 missing-manufacturer sales as the adverse inference rate was upheld.

Commerce's substitution of the actual sales prices for the 28,000 sales missing manufacturer information with the highest non-aberrational net price among those 28,000 sales was a reasonable application of adverse facts available based on Salzgitter's failure to cooperate to the best of its ability
14012: Commerce properly applied adverse facts available under 19 U.S.C. § 1677e(a) and (b) because Chandan failed to provide requested window-period sales data and did not cooperate to the best of its ability.
we do not second-guess Commerce's decision to use facts otherwise available and adverse inferences in the case at hand.
14013: Commerce properly applied total, rather than partial, adverse facts available because the sales and costs data deficiencies were pervasive and fundamental.
we conclude that substantial evidence supports Commerce's decision to use total, rather than partial, AFA.
14014: Commerce's selection of the 145.25% dumping margin, taken from the same underlying investigation and corroborated, was within its discretion and not punitive.

There is no abuse of discretion because Commerce acted within its statutory authority by selecting a margin that was (1) applied in the same underlying investigation; and (2) corroborated against Chandan's own product-specific margins.
14142: Commerce's use of total adverse facts available (AFA) against Unicatch after it failed to provide a complete cost reconciliation, held supported by substantial evidence.
Commerce's application of total FA and AFA in this case is supported by substantial evidence.
14143: Commerce's selection of the 78.17% petition rate as the AFA rate for Unicatch, corroborated by transaction-specific margins; held supported by substantial evidence.
We find that substantial evidence supports Commerce's application of the 78.17% AFA rate.
14191: AD/CVD adverse facts available: Commerce's adverse inference selecting the 154.33% petition rate under 19 U.S.C. 1677e(b) was unsupported by substantial evidence and an abuse of discretion.
applying an adverse inference to select the 154.33% rate was unsupported by the required substantial evidence and was an abuse of discretion
14418: Whether Customs properly applied an adverse inference against the foreign manufacturers under 19 U.S.C. § 1517(c)(3) for their failure to cooperate, and whether it was proper despite the importers' own cooperation; held the adverse inference was in accordance with law.

Because it is uncontroverted that the alleged manufacturers were not cooperative, Customs properly applied an adverse inference against the manufacturer as authorized by statute, irrespective of the conduct of other interested parties like Appellants.
14580: AD/CVD surrogate value selection for coal-based carbonized material (HS 4402.90.1000 coconut shell charcoal vs. HS 4402.90 wood charcoal); Commerce's surrogate value choice upheld as supported by substantial evidence

What is critical is the statement in the first sentence of the paragraph that, in the past, "Commerce found coconut shell charcoal to be the best available information with which to value mandatory respondents' coal-based [carbonized material] based on the reported product specifications."
15021: Adverse facts available and adverse inference under 19 U.S.C. 1677e: Commerce's use of total AFA with an adverse inference (41.04% rate) was reasonable and supported by substantial evidence.

we hold that Commerce's determination to resort to total AFA including an adverse inference to establish Corinth's dumping margin was reasonable, supported by substantial evidence, and otherwise not contrary to law.
15048: AD/CVD adverse facts available / separate-rate determination: Commerce's assignment of the PRC-wide rate to Pirelli China for failing to demonstrate independence from government control was upheld
